item.title: Recent cases heard at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Recent cases heard at King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court
King’s Lynn Magistrates’ Court dealt with a series of cases last week involving theft, driving offences, and arson. Among those appearing were several prolific shoplifters, including James Leonard, who reached his 200th recorded offence after stealing items from a local store. Other defendants faced sentencing for supermarket thefts in Downham, Sheringham, and Fakenham.
The court also addressed driving offences, including individuals caught without valid licences or insurance, and a case of arson at the St James Multi-Storey Car Park. Additionally, magistrates heard cases involving public order offences, drug possession, and the assault of a police officer. Defendants received various penalties, ranging from fines and community orders to custodial sentences.

item.title: King’s Lynn Town Hall to host memorial lecture on Margery Kempe
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn Town Hall to host memorial lecture on Margery Kempe
King’s Lynn Town Hall will host the 12th annual Pat Midgley Memorial Lecture on Thursday, November 19. Organised by True’s Yard Fisherfolk Museum, the event runs from 7pm to 8pm in the Stone Hall and will be hosted by the Mayor of West Norfolk, Councillor Steve Bearshaw.
Speakers Mirabelle Dominé-Walley and Luke Walker will present a lecture and film titled "Margery Kempe and the Wash." The presentation examines the life of the medieval mystic alongside traditional fishing practices on the Wash. Tickets are priced at £5 and include refreshments. The lecture honours the late Pat Midgley, who founded the museum and helped preserve historic fisherfolk cottages in the town.

item.title: New book examines the impact of the 1643 Siege of King’s Lynn
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
New book examines the impact of the 1643 Siege of King’s Lynn
A new book by local historian James Rye explores the long-term consequences of the 1643 Civil War siege of King’s Lynn. Titled "The Siege of King’s Lynn 1643: A Port Divided and the Cost of Civil War," the work details how the three-week conflict affected trade, property repairs, and the lives of local residents.
Mr Rye utilised contemporary records and archaeological research to document the challenges faced by the town following its negotiated surrender. The book features historical figures including Thomas Toll and Alice L’Estrange. It is currently available for purchase online, priced at £7.99 for the paperback edition or £4.99 for the eBook.
🔗 More details: https://www.lynnnews.co.uk/news/new-book-explores-town-s-civil-war-siege-and-its-lasting-imp-9488704/

item.description:

Queen Elizabeth Hospital receives £3.9m for winter urgent care
The Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn has been awarded £3.9 million in government funding to boost urgent and emergency care services. The investment aims to help the hospital manage increased demand during the winter months by allowing staff to treat minor illnesses and injuries separately from emergency cases.
Work to reconfigure the emergency department is already underway, with plans for a new urgent treatment centre to follow. Local MPs Terry Jermy and James Wild have welcomed the funding, though both continue to press for long-term commitments regarding the future of the hospital’s 24/7 A&E department. This grant is part of a wider £140 million national investment across 14 urgent care schemes in England.

item.title: Concerns grow over potential maternity service changes in Norfolk
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Concerns grow over potential maternity service changes in Norfolk
Campaigners and MPs have raised concerns over the future of maternity services at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn and the James Paget Hospital in Gorleston. Both sites are among the smallest consultant-led units in England, and hospital bosses are currently reviewing healthcare strategies due to factors including falling birth rates.
While the Norfolk and Waveney University Hospitals Group insists no decisions have been made, there are fears that downgrading these units could force women to travel longer distances for care. Local leaders have argued that services should remain accessible and locally based. The clinical strategy is expected to be presented to the Norfolk County Council’s health overview and scrutiny committee next month.

Stem cell donor event held in King’s Lynn for baby Reuben
The East of England Ambulance Service is hosting a stem cell swabbing event today at the Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King’s Lynn. The drive aims to find a life-saving donor for Reuben, a baby boy from Norfolk who was diagnosed with acute myeloid leukaemia at ten months old.
Staff are welcoming potential donors at the ambulance station on Gayton Road until 6pm this evening. Those aged between 16 and 55 are encouraged to attend for a simple cheek swab to join the DKMS and Anthony Nolan registers. Anyone unable to visit the hospital site can also register online to request a home testing kit. Every new registration increases the chances of finding a match for Reuben and other patients worldwide.

New DC horror film Clay Face arrives at The Light in Wisbech
A new addition to the DC Universe is now showing at The Light cinema in Wisbech. The film, titled Clay Face, is an R-rated origin story focusing on the iconic Batman villain. It stars Tom Rhys Harries as Matt Hagen, an actor who undergoes an experimental nanite treatment after a brutal attack. The cast also features Naomi Ackie, Max Minghella, and Rob Brydon. While the film explores themes of vengeance and body horror, it has received praise for its performances and emotional depth. Local cinema-goers can catch the movie at the Wisbech venue now.

item.title: New management team takes over King’s Lynn hair and beauty salon
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
New management team takes over King’s Lynn hair and beauty salon
A new team is now in charge at the House of Hair and Beauty on Tower Street in King’s Lynn. Manager Cole Ellis, who has over two decades of industry experience, is working alongside stylist Karyn Hardy to offer a range of hair treatments. The salon is currently looking to recruit additional stylists to fill available chairs and a beauty room.
The business is located next to the Majestic Cinema and is open Tuesday to Saturday, from 9am until 5pm, with flexible late appointments available. New clients are currently being offered a 30 percent discount on treatments. Mr Ellis says he aims to create a welcoming, family-like atmosphere for both staff and customers.
